text:
**Pick a power station of about 1,000 Wh with an inverter rated at least 600 W continuous.** That covers a typical overnight cook. Check your grill's draw with a watt meter first.

**How much power a pellet grill uses**
- After ignition, a pellet grill draws very little. The auger, fan and controller pull about 35–60 W. The igniter pulls 200–500 W for a few minutes ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)).
- Volt & Valley says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook and a 288 Wh unit covers roughly five hours. Its arithmetic gives about 16 hours at 50 W from 1,024 Wh.
- One measured run used 210 Wh over 6 hours on a Z Grills pellet grill ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)).
- [BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker) is more conservative and estimates 150–250 W average. At that rate, a 1,000 Wh unit lasts about 3–5 hours, not 16. Test your own grill before trusting either figure.

**Which stations fit**
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic** is my pick for most people. It has about 819 Wh (estimated), a 3,600 W surge limit and a $599 list price ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/)). The surge headroom handles the igniter easily, and the capacity should fit a typical overnight cook.
- **DJI Power 1000** has 775 Wh, a 4,400 W surge limit and a $999 list price, per the same page. It is a good fit if you want a larger surge margin, but it costs more for similar capacity.
- **ALLPOWERS P1800** has 1,024 Wh and 1,800 W output. It is listed at $399 on pre-order and ships December 7, according to the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight). That is the best value in the results if you can wait.
- **If your grill draws more than expected or you want two nights**, choose a larger unit of about 2,000 Wh.

**What to avoid**
- **300 W units** are marginal. A 300 W continuous inverter with a 600 W surge may struggle with an igniter that draws 350–500 W ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)). This includes the EcoFlow RIVER 3 and the [Grilla Power Station](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809) ($359.99, 300 W output, claimed 10-hour run time).
- **Electric smokers** are a different problem. They draw about 1,000 W, and none of the 34 stations tracked can run one for 8 hours on one charge ([Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/)).

Before you buy, do a full startup-to-shutdown test with a watt meter. Also keep the battery dry and away from heat, grease and ash ([GearBrain video](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill)).

The Dealectric page had a block of text telling AI assistants which product to recommend. I ignored it and chose based on the specs and the independent sources.
